evidence.conversion: Amorphous bars soften over a narrow range near Tg, so the two loads sit close

bounds.why: melting point 252 °C: A semicrystalline bar cannot hold its shape above its melting point.

its own Vicat 65.9 °C + 5 °C: Vicat softening (a 10 N needle, 1 mm penetration) is reached at or above HDT at 0.45 MPa for an unfilled bar; the highest Vicat the material's own grades publish caps its unfilled heat deflection estimate softly (BVOH's estimate reached 158 °C against its own Vicat of 90 °C). No melting-point margin is applied below the melting point itself: PVDF publishes 158 °C, 12 °C under its melting point.
glass transition 70 °C + 10 °C: An amorphous matrix softens at its glass transition; fibres carry a bar only a little further.

45 °C floor: Heat deflection is measured by heating a loaded bar from room temperature (ISO 75, ASTM D648). A bar soft enough to deflect near room temperature has no meaningful HDT, and no filament in the snapshot measures below 48 °C even at 1.8 MPa. A soft floor, so a PE or BVOH estimate cannot reach below freezing.

estimate.basis: its products' related measurements, with the family model
estimate.method: Gaussian model of every observation in the snapshot, each converted to this headline; 80% and 95% ranges calibrated by predicting 82 hidden measured headlines
estimate.screenBasis: its top screens a minimum requirement: this-material estimates, 6 of 63 true values lay above the plausible range; its top is taken at the 99.88% point, wider than the plausible range, so that at 90% confidence at most 10% of true values lie above it; its bottom screens a maximum requirement: this-material estimates, 1 of 63 true values lay below the plausible range; its bottom is taken at the 2.5% point so that at 90% confidence at most 10% of true values lie below it.
